back_translation: Gather yourselves together, gather, O nation that knows no shame,
before the decree takes effect and the day passes away like blown chaff, before the fierce anger of the LORD comes upon you, before the day of the LORD's anger comes upon you.
Seek the LORD, all you humble of the land who carry out His ordinances. Seek righteousness; seek humility. Perhaps you will be sheltered on the day of the LORD's anger.
For Gaza will be forsaken and Ashkelon left a desolation. Ashdod's people will be driven out at noon, and Ekron will be uprooted.
Woe to the inhabitants of the seacoast, O nation of the Cherethites! The word of the LORD is against you: O Canaan, land of the Philistines, 'I will destroy you until no inhabitant remains.'
The seacoast will become pastures, with wells for shepherds and folds for sheep.

That coast will belong to the remnant of the house of Judah; there they will graze their flocks. In the evening they will lie down among the houses of Ashkelon, for the LORD their God will attend to them and restore them to their former state.
'I have heard the taunts of Moab and the insults of the Ammonites, who taunted My people and made boasts against their border.

'Therefore, declares the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, as surely as I live, Moab will become like Sodom and the Ammonites like Gomorrah—a place of nettles and salt pits, a perpetual wasteland. The remnant of My people will plunder them, and the rest of My nation will inherit them.'
This will come upon them in return for their pride, because they taunted and made themselves great against the people of the LORD of Hosts.
The LORD will be terrifying to them, for He will starve all the gods of the earth; then people will bow down to Him, each from his own place—all the coastlands of the nations.
'You too, O Cushites, will be slain by My sword.'
He will stretch out His hand against the north and destroy Assyria; He will make Nineveh a desolation, dry as the desert.

Herds will lie down in her midst, beasts of every kind. Both the pelican and the owl will roost on her pillar-tops. A voice will sound in the window; desolation will be on the threshold, for the cedar paneling has been laid bare.

This is the exultant city that dwelt securely, that said in her heart, 'I am, and there is none besides me.' How she has become a desolation, a lair for beasts! Everyone who passes by her hisses and shakes his fist.
